reasons: The claimed deviation is supported by the cited text: Section 9(b) contains substantive warranties (industry standards, error-free, Laws compliance) running for the Term, and Section 13's disclaimer expressly carves out warranties 'set forth in this Agreement', so the only real gap is the absence of any express remedy and of a professional/workmanlike performance standard — exactly what the redline addresses.

The insert is minimal and correctly located: a new sub-clause (xii) appended after existing (xi) in p0041, continuing the existing numbering of the Section 9(b) list, with no unnecessary rewriting of surrounding text or of the disclaimer (which needs no change given the express carve-out).

The added language reaches the playbook position: workmanlike/industry-standard performance warranty plus repair, replacement, re-performance or refund of fees, and it is expressly non-exclusive of Customer's other rights, which is more favorable to us than the model language's default.

The failed deterministic check on a 90-day/12-month period is a phrasing artifact, not a substantive defect — the existing warranties run 'throughout the Term' with no expiry, which exceeds the preferred 12-month/90-day durations, so no period needs to be inserted.

The comment is accurate, correctly attributes the change to the missing warranty remedy, cites the playbook position, concedes the Vendor-option point as a sensible fallback, and complies with the required prefix and concise first-person-plural tone.

Minor, non-blocking: embedding the remedy sentence inside warranty item (xii) is structurally awkward (a remedy housed in a list of warranties); a standalone sentence after the list would read more cleanly, but the drafting is unambiguous and enforceable as written.
